author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Menlo Security's logs are pull only, through the Menlo Log API, so these parsers read the events the example bridge in bridges/menlo-security-logs polls and posts to HTTP Ingest, with "menlo_record" (the log type) first. Give the bridge an Admin Portal API token with only the Log Export API permission. Menlo's Log API reference needs a sign-in, so the field names come from Menlo's own Microsoft Sentinel connector, which lists the web, audit and bandwidth fields, and the event shape from the Cortex XSOAR Menlo Security pack. Web logs (page_request, file_download, proxy_event, application_request) go to HTTP, with x-client-ip as the source, xff_ip as the true source, origin_ip or dst as the destination, userid as the user (Unknown is left out), and the URL, method, response code, user agent and referer. pe_action block is blocked; allow, isolate (rendered in isolation), direct and the rest are allowed. The policy rule and reason, categories, threat type, risk score, file name, hash, size and scan result, egress address, countries, proxy event detail and session go to event_metadata. Menlo writes NA for a value it doesn't have, which the parsers leave out, and a field with several values as a list, of which the first three are joined. Admin audit logs go to CloudAudit, with the first of audit_actions as the event name, sub_event_type as the event type, uid as the user, and details and additional_info, which are JSON text, as request parameters. Menlo publishes no example of an audit event, so the audit samples use the field names in Menlo's connector with made-up values, and the actions and event types in them are inferred. Event times have no zone and are read as UTC, as Menlo's connector does. Other log types the bridge can read, such as email, dlp or bandwidth, stay at the parent as generic records. Samples follow those field lists with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (120 of 120 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs, the email line at the parent included), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (118 of 118 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser claimed these records.
